checks.evidence: 116 silver rows against 116 legacy psv lines; 15 quarantined rows. 14 of them are expectation failures and all 14 are still in silver. The 15th is the HDR-shadowed record, which the legacy sed deletes before parsing, so it is absent from the legacy output too and quarantine reports it with psv_line NULL and failed_expectations ['not_hdr_trl_shadowed']. Every expectation is warn-only (expect_all), so no expectation removes a record from silver or from gold's input (contract C-6.3, P2-D02).

comparison_note: The compared column is psv_line, the whole legacy output line byte for byte, keyed by (source_file, record_no). Field-level comparison is deliberately not used: the legacy's positional '|' split and the target's byte slices disagree by design on the delimiter-collision record (C-5.1), so a field diff there would measure the comparison, not the parse.

idempotency_rerun.evidence: pipeline update 8d500c0e-10b6-4685-b9ec-dff3f1b20a56, rerun from the committed source after the review fixes; silver 116 rows / md5 115f7e40240d7529b6bc48ec0a922ccd, quarantine 15 rows / md5 cde9f90726dcbf5300535477ccdfea66, trailer audit 6 rows / md5 c286f2cd16e1168b779e31521c768835 - identical before and after (idempotency.before.json, idempotency.after.json). Silver is byte-identical to the pre-review-fix runs; only quarantine grew, by the one shadowed record.

planted_anomaly_detections.compared_as: set of (expectation, rows failing it) over ow_tp.bronze.custbill_quarantine, per the frozen tolerances
planted_anomaly_detections.quarantine_locator: Every quarantine row carries byte_offset, the zero-based offset of the record's first byte in its landed file, so a reader can seek straight to it; records are not fixed length in practice, so record_no alone does not locate one. Checked two ways: test_byte_offsets_locate_the_record slices every captured file at the computed offsets, and the pipeline's window sum over custbill_raw returns the same values (record 15 of CUSTBILL_PROBE_001.dat at 805).
planted_anomaly_detections.derivation: expected_set enumerated by hand from databricks/migration/p2/baseline/gen_probe_fixture.py before the quarantine table was read: the short, long and blank records plus the UTF-8 and CRLF probes are the five over/under-length records; the UTF-8 record's multibyte name shifts date, currency and rec_type into the neighbouring fields, which is why those counts exceed the number of deliberately bad values.

trailer_audit.finding: CUSTBILL_PROBE_001.dat declares a trailer of 15 and parses 14: the record whose customer id starts HDRFAKE is deleted by the legacy sed as if it were a header. The target reproduces that loss exactly (C-4.1/C-4.2) and surfaces it in ow_tp.bronze.custbill_trailer_audit as shadowed_count=1 instead of silently swallowing it. Audit only - it never changes output. The record is also attributed individually in ow_tp.bronze.custbill_quarantine, with its byte offset and failed_expectations ['not_hdr_trl_shadowed'], so the loss is traceable to a record and not only to a per-file count.

unverified_paths: P2-D01, the landing race: the legacy poller can parse a half-written .dat, the target lands atomically and sequences parse behind it. Named behaviour change, not exercisable against pinned inputs.
Structure parity: the harness compares rows, not Delta table properties, clustering, comments or grants. Nothing checks that ow_tp.silver grants match any legacy access model.

Expectation semantics: the ten expectations are new quality signals with no legacy counterpart. They are warn-only by construction, so the harness proves they do not filter, but nothing external validates the thresholds themselves.

The legacy parser is reconciled through its captured output over the pinned fixture set. Inputs outside that set - other encodings, records longer than the probes, other delimiter placements - are not exercised.
parsed_at and quarantined_at are target-side wall clock with no legacy counterpart and are excluded from both the keyed diff and the idempotency fingerprint.
